title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is faint pencil with a few blue-ink additions and is largely illegible, so this reading is tentative. It sits in a folder that also holds a chapter of Grothendieck's own manuscript on relative analytic groups (previous page) and a page from Sullivan's English text on minimal models and the lower central series of π1 (next page, 'N27', p.108). That placement suggests the 1976 IHÉS lecture was meant to compare a divided-power (PD) de Rham complex with Sullivan's de Rham algebra / rational homotopy theory.

What can be made out:
- Heading: 'Détermination de ...' (struck words), then something like 'Disposition de Ω^{**} = Γ_1(G_a) ⊗ Â_1 ...'. This appears to be the PD de Rham complex of the affine line, i.e. divided-power polynomials in one variable T together with dT, possibly completed and augmented: Â_1^{**+}.
- Phrases such as 'l'Algèbre de De Rham', 'algèbres augmentées', 'différentielles' and '... T'. The task seems to be to determine morphisms of augmented differential (bi)graded PD algebras Â_1^{**+} → Â_n^{**+} (or to Â_0). Such a morphism is fixed by the image ξ of the coordinate T, subject to the condition that it respect divided powers and the differential (a normalisation 'φ(1)=1' is visible).
- Coface maps Δ_0 → Δ_1 are written as two maps ('φ, β' or φ^0, φ^1) with φ^0(ξ_0)=1 and φ^1(ξ_0)=0, i.e. evaluation at the two endpoints of the 1-simplex.
- Δ_2 → Δ_1 and the conditions φ_0(0)=0, φ_0(1)=φ_1(0), φ_1(1)=1 describe two consecutive 'paths' glued end to end, i.e. a concatenation or subdivision of the interval.
- The boxed bottom formulas expand products such as φ_0(ξ_0)φ_1(ξ_0) and relations like φ_0(ξ_0)... = φ_1(...); they look like compatibility identities for this composition.

The overall aim appears to be a cosimplicial (or path-space / interval-object) structure on PD de Rham algebras of standard simplices, Δ_n ↦ PD-de Rham complex of the n-simplex. This would be an integral or characteristic-p analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms ∇(p,•). It would allow a de Rham-style algebraic model of homotopy types beyond Q, the PD structure making the Poincaré lemma hold integrally.
errors: Too illegible to check the computations; no evident error in the legible fragments (the endpoint and gluing conditions are consistent).

ideas.what: PD (divided power) de Rham complex of the affine line Γ(G_a)⊗Λ(dT), augmented and possibly completed, used as an 'interval object'.
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on simplices; integral analogue of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial forms A_PL
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) for rational forms; Cenkl–Porter (c.1980–81) for forms with controlled denominators; Berthelot / Illusie for the PD de Rham complex in crystalline cohomology
ideas.where_published: Unpublished 1976 IHÉS lecture; not in EGA/SGA, as far as I know

ideas.what: Cosimplicial structure: coface maps Δ0→Δ1 as evaluation at endpoints (ξ↦1, ξ↦0), and Δ2→Δ1 maps encoding concatenation of paths.
ideas.modern_name: Cosimplicial commutative DG algebra of forms on standard simplices; simplicial de Rham functor

missed.claim: Grothendieck appears to have sought a cosimplicial PD de Rham algebra as an integral or char-p replacement for Sullivan's rational de Rham models, in direct dialogue with Sullivan's text filed alongside. Integral or p-adic algebraic models of homotopy types were later approached differently (Cenkl–Porter tame homotopy; Mandell's E∞ cochains, 2001/2006). A PD-de Rham simplicial approach remains marginal in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This idea links crystalline / PD methods to integral homotopy theory, a link now revisited via derived de Rham cohomology and p-adic homotopy theory. Grothendieck's early attempt is undocumented.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly illegible and its fragments are routine cosimplicial bookkeeping. The interest lies in the context: a 1976 Grothendieck attempt to make divided-power de Rham algebras of simplices an integral version of Sullivan's theory, which is not widely known.
transcription_corrections: Heading likely 'Détermination de ...' with struck word; second line likely 'Disposition de Ω^{**}_{...} = Γ_1(G_a) ⊗ Â_1 ...' (Γ = divided power algebra).
Coface conditions read φ^0(ξ_0)=1, φ^1(ξ_0)=0 with maps Δ_0 → Δ_1.
